stories.headline: Banxico cuts benchmark rate 25bp to 6.50%, signals end of two-year easing cycle
stories.summary: In a 3-2 divided vote on May 7, Banco de México reduced its reference rate to 6.50%, the lowest since March 2022, and explicitly signaled this would be the final cut of the current easing cycle begun in early 2024. Governors Heath and Borja dissented; the central bank simultaneously revised inflation forecasts upward for Q2-Q3 2026. The peso oscillated then strengthened, ending the week near two-year highs against the dollar.

stories.headline: SEMAR records fourth consecutive cocaine seizure in Pacific waters off Guerrero, 89 bales total in one week
stories.summary: The Mexican Navy's Secretariat (SEMAR) completed its fourth consecutive drug interdiction in a week off Guerrero's Pacific coast on May 9, seizing 26 bales of suspected cocaine from a small vessel and arresting two foreign nationals. The four operations together netted 89 bales, which authorities described as a significant financial blow to organized crime.

stories.headline: Sheinbaum's Sonora working tour: IMSS hospital inauguration, Yaqui land decree, Seri aqueduct, Canal de Navojoa
stories.summary: President Sheinbaum conducted a multi-day working trip to Sonora on May 9, inaugurating the IMSS Hospital General de Zona No. 15 in Hermosillo (1.03 billion peso investment), signing a new land restitution decree for the Yaqui people (bringing total to 45,500 hectares), inaugurating the Seri-Comca'ac aqueduct in Punta Chueca, and completing the first stage of the Canal Principal de Navojoa (6.5 billion peso investment). The trip also included CNTE teacher protests at one event.

stories.headline: Rocha Moya faces US cartel-nexus accusations, house attacked; federal security cabinet defends record
stories.summary: Sinaloa Governor-on-leave Rubén Rocha Moya was named in a US Justice Department investigation alongside nine other officials for alleged ties to Los Chapitos. On May 9, an armed attack was carried out against a property linked to Rocha Moya in Culiacán. Security Secretary García Harfuch stated the federal government had no prior intelligence linking Rocha Moya to organized crime, and confirmed Rocha Moya retained federal security protection. The case triggered sustained opposition attacks on Morena.

stories.headline: Madrid regional president Díaz Ayuso's visit to Mexico sparks political controversy, cuts trip short
stories.summary: Isabel Díaz Ayuso, president of the Community of Madrid, provoked weeks of diplomatic friction during an institutional visit to Mexico (May 4–9) during which she paid tribute to Hernán Cortés and criticized the Sheinbaum government's trajectory. She cut her trip short citing a 'climate of boycott', while a private cultural group denied receiving any pressure from the Mexican government to uninvite her. Sheinbaum responded by criticizing Mexican opposition parties for hosting the visit, and the left-wing Más Madrid coalition sent a public apology letter to Sheinbaum.

stories.headline: García Harfuch profile surges: 'Batman' of Mexican security emerges as prospective 2030 presidential figure
stories.summary: Multiple domestic and international outlets published feature profiles of Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch this week, referencing his survival of a 400-round CJNG assassination attempt and the February killing of cartel boss 'El Mencho'. Articles from Chile, Paraguay, Colombia, and Mexico assess him as a rising political figure with possible 2030 presidential ambitions, and a reality TV producer publicly invited him to join La Casa de los Famosos.

stories.headline: SSPC agents attacked in Culiacán during operation against 'Mayito Flaco' cell; two aggressors killed, one detained
stories.summary: Federal security forces under García Harfuch were ambushed by armed civilians in the outskirts of Culiacán, Sinaloa on approximately May 8 while investigating a kidnapping cell linked to the 'Mayito Flaco' faction of the Sinaloa cartel. Two aggressors were killed and one detained. García Harfuch reported the incident via social media, stating operations in the area were continuing.

stories.headline: Mother's Day protests: families of the disappeared march, demand meeting with Sheinbaum
stories.summary: On Mexico's Mother's Day (May 10), thousands marched in Mexico City led by collectives of mothers searching for disappeared relatives, with over 130,000 people officially missing nationwide. Ahead of the march, organizations formally demanded Sheinbaum meet with them; a PAN congressmember and a Morena-era open letter to the president also demanded action on enforced disappearances. Sheinbaum issued no public commitment to meet.

stories.summary: President Sheinbaum used Mother's Day (May 10) to launch/expand the Pensión Mujeres Bienestar program at a large event in Cajeme, Sonora, benefiting 3 million women nationwide and approximately 70,000 in Sonora. She made statements declaring violence against women was 'finished' and promoted gender equality rhetoric amid contrasting news of the disappeared-persons march in Mexico City.

stories.headline: PEMEX restructuring eliminates ~40 subsidiaries; Gasolinas Bienestar renamed amid Cuba fuel controversy
stories.summary: President Sheinbaum announced on May 7-8 that PEMEX would absorb virtually all of its approximately 40 subsidiaries into the core corporate structure, retaining only three or four. The announcement surfaced a renamed subsidiary—now called Servicios Logísticos Integrales Mumiya—which had been exporting fuel to Cuba, prompting questions about the bilateral commercial arrangement valued at $500 million annually.

stories.headline: FGR wins extinction-of-domain case over former PEMEX director Lozoya's 51 million-peso mansion
stories.summary: A Mexican federal appeals court upheld the FGR's extinction-of-domain claim over a property in Lomas de Bezares (Mexico City) linked to former PEMEX director Emilio Lozoya, valued at 51.7 million pesos. The court confirmed the residence was purchased with illicit funds tied to the Agronitrogenados bribery scandal, in which PEMEX overpaid 275 million dollars for a fertilizer plant during Lozoya's tenure.
